problem: An elongated hard-surface detail must merge into a curved SubD host without a detached strip, an abrupt crease, or global support-loop propagation.
source_observation: The tutorial cleans and reroutes the cut boundary, creates a local buffer, fades detail depth to flush, terminates loops in a low-stress region, and relaxes curved-border spacing.
controlled_failure: Full relief begins on one radial ring; the fixed MatCap view shows a hard horizontal pinch.
correction: Relief influence is ramped across successive rings while the host remains one connected 16-segment all-quad cage with live Solidify and SubD.
transfer: A different 14-segment oval cuff routes a diagonal relief by blending both depth and lateral column influence. The first column-jumping attempt was rejected for waviness; the retained transfer has zero automated pinch candidates.
promoted_rule: On a curved SubD host, fade integrated-detail displacement continuously in every changing grid direction and inspect fixed MatCap highlights; do not infer success from topology validity or pinch-candidate count alone.
non_rule: Triangles or poles are not universally required, forbidden, or automatically safe. Their placement must be tested against local curvature and highlight flow.
limitations: The source-like asset uses a regular radial grid rather than reproducing the tutorial's exact Boolean cleanup and local triangle termination.
The source thumbnail, not independent timestamp frames, is the non-Gemini visual check.
The transfer validates a diagonal relief on one additional surface family, not arbitrary curved hosts.
